title: What would change a choice, and who bears it
note: Each of Chapters 1 to 28 ends its argument with the evidence that would change its choice, and says who bears the choice's cost. They are quoted here as the chapters write them: the conditions grouped by the kind of evidence they name, the costs by who bears them. A sentence that names several appears under each.

conditions.title: An alternative that serves as well

entries.title: The Child With Nobody
entries.heading: Argument: Standing before identity
entries.text: I would reconsider on either of two findings: that verification can run, among many unregistered people, beside a fallback that keeps every legitimate claimant served while identity is checked; or that standing by encounter lets duplicate claims grow until genuine claimants go without essentials. Either would reverse the comparison this choice rests on.

entries.title: What the Record May Say
entries.heading: Argument: Why the record is closed by name
entries.text: I would reconsider if integrated records with contest before effect and independent review were shown, for the people least able to contest, to produce fewer wrongful adverse decisions than purpose-bound records, or if people whose need sat in one office's file were shown to go unfound for want of a joined account.

entries.title: What You Are Owed
entries.heading: Argument: Owed to everyone, by someone
entries.text: I would reconsider the named goods if cash brought shelter, care and company to people who cannot manage money, a small child or an adult in crisis, as reliably as provision does.

entries.title: What You Are Owed
entries.heading: Argument: Owed to everyone, by someone
entries.text: I would reconsider the unconditional debt only on evidence that a test of inability can be run without shutting out the people it exists to reach.

entries.title: Whether It Arrived
entries.heading: Argument: Evidence from the person served
entries.text: I would reconsider if witnessed receipts proved easy to forge in concert at scale, if providers were found holding back delivery until a witness could attend, or if authentication with an assured fallback of serving first were shown to turn away nobody entitled.

entries.title: Who Owes, and What Follows
entries.heading: Argument: Named bearers, and a court that secures the minimum
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that deferential review reaches people in desperate need as reliably as a declared minimum, or that declared plans and interim orders secure essentials no faster than ordinary budgets.

entries.title: An Ordinary Week
entries.heading: Argument: Power that must write before it touches
entries.text: I would reconsider on two findings together: that requiring a complete record before a protective act lets serious harm through that discretion would have stopped, and that discretion checked only after the fact falls evenly on the people it touches and is corrected when it errs.

entries.title: What Nobody Has to Ask Permission For
entries.heading: Argument: Two grounds and an end
entries.text: I would reopen the list only on evidence that an open purpose test, applied by independent reviewers, protects dissent and unpopular belief as reliably as two fixed grounds while answering those injuries too.

entries.title: Work, Pay and Contribution
entries.heading: Argument: Work above the floor
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that a work condition with a hardship exception moves people into lasting work without the debt and ill health the Welfare Conditionality project recorded, and without the discretion the auditors found; and I would narrow the control test if written terms proved to track who controls the work as reliably as the facts do.

entries.title: What Money Cannot Buy
entries.heading: Argument: Ownership under the floor, borrowing under law
entries.text: I would reconsider requiring a finding if people who depend on a gate repeatedly waited longer than the harm lasted, while thresholds reached the same gates with few mistaken designations.

entries.title: The Same Route for Everyone
entries.heading: Argument: Effects, adjustments and measures that end
entries.text: I would reconsider the measures if continuation findings kept renewing them while the disadvantage stayed where it was, or if identical treatment with accessibility and accommodation removed a disadvantage as quickly.

entries.title: A Place in Which Life Remains Possible
entries.heading: Argument: Conditions kept apart
entries.text: Evidence that advisory offices alone secured review before irreversible commitments would favour removing the pause.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: I would reconsider if welfare regimes were shown to prevent severe avoidable suffering as reliably where owners or industries gain from it, or if a separate Advocate were shown to be captured by the uses it watches or to stall decisions a single office would make better.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: Evidence that the food rule left people short of adequate food despite the floor, or that humane standards reliably spared farmed animals severe suffering in life and at death, would favour narrowing the food rule.

entries.title: Holding a Role in Somebody's Life
entries.heading: Argument: Support before substitution
entries.text: I would reconsider if people whose will could not be read after support came to more harm under a best-interpretation route than comparable people under best-interests decisions, or if support-first left needed decisions waiting; no study comparing the two in practice is cited here, so the choice rests on how each is built.

entries.title: Arriving and Belonging
entries.heading: Argument: The person before the status
entries.text: I would reconsider the firewall if people without papers used services as readily where enforcement reads service records as where it cannot; the residence line if former residents stayed as bound by a place's decisions as the people living there, or if a workable institution gave people affected from outside a say without taking the government's accountability from those it governs; and the consent line if harms classed as reversible repeatedly proved permanent once consultation had let them proceed.

entries.title: Answerability and Authority
entries.heading: Argument: Answerable for good, empowered for now
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that hearing-first orders, decided promptly, protect people who expose officials from retaliatory prosecution as reliably as protection that starts with the exposure, while delaying fewer unrelated cases.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Argument: Divided without deadlock
entries.text: I would reconsider the council if collective executives under the same limits missed lawful deadlines more often than cabinets; the Regions Council if protected competence and judicial review alone kept regional self-government secure; and divided appointments if records showed one coalition directing the separate sources, or if elected confirmation kept reviewers as independent at lower cost.

entries.title: The Vote Conviction Does Not Take
entries.heading: Argument: The vote outside the sentence
entries.text: I would reconsider if disenfranchisement fitted by a judge to each offence were shown to cut reoffending or protect elections while falling evenly across groups.

entries.title: What May Be Kept About You
entries.heading: Argument: Uses bound to their holding, decisions to a person
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that automatic propagation, with contest before effect, produced fewer wrongful adverse decisions and fewer missed entitlements than holdings bound to one purpose. I would begin by letting a favourable automated change take effect on one actor's record, with a reviewer able to withdraw it, as a person's own access request already does.

entries.title: A Crisis Does Not Suspend the Republic
entries.heading: Argument: Four powers and every right in force
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that emergencies bring needs that no hazard-specific, reviewable measure can meet but an Article 4 derogation can, with the derogation ending on time and review correcting its errors. Oren Gross and Fionnuala Ní Aoláin's comparative study of three models of the law's response to crisis, from the Roman republic to the responses to the London attacks of July 2005, is where I would look.

entries.title: Changing the Rules
entries.heading: Argument: A fixed core behind an open route
entries.text: I would reconsider if readings of the core repeatedly blocked reforms that kept its protections whole, if the route repeatedly stalled rights-preserving reforms with majority support, or if constitutions without a fixed core proved as reliable at keeping the losers of a political contest able to live, dissent and seek correction.

entries.title: A Prisoner Is a Person
entries.heading: Argument: Liberty is what a sentence takes
entries.text: I would reconsider if prisons that owed the people they hold the whole floor as a constitutional debt were shown to hold them less safely, or to see more reoffending after release, than systems that suspended those claims for the sentence; or if the floor owed inside prisons were shown to come out of what the people they harmed receive.

entries.title: Where People Are Put
entries.heading: Argument: Proved harm opens the harshest place
entries.text: I would reconsider if people whose harms fell below the line were shown repeatedly to cause grave harm from less restrictive places that a secure place would have prevented, and if a scored assessment predicted that harm accurately and evenly across groups.

entries.title: The One Thing Taken
entries.heading: Argument: A power that takes movement and then expires
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence from outside Norway that confinement's protective gains vanish or reverse; on evidence that measures short of confinement protect people from further grave harm as well, in the cases where adjudicators now find them insufficient; on evidence that a bounded power grows despite its bounds, as Gilmore describes; and on evidence that lapses recur despite the duty to review, which would call for earlier review rather than automatic extension.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Argument: Findings from outside the walls
entries.text: I would reconsider on evidence that inspections run by holding institutions find and correct denied contact as often and as fast as independent visiting bodies, judged by what detained people report, or that independent findings come so slowly that people stay isolated longer than internal correction would leave them. The two texts I rely on state a standard; a study comparing the two kinds of inspection could settle the question.

entries.title: The Shield
entries.heading: Argument: Protection that follows the charge
entries.text: Reviewers who wrongly find a prosecution unrelated open the way to confinement, someone who controls the appointment records can manufacture that finding, and protection for a disclosure made before the charge depends on two witnesses dating it honestly; the waits the rule imposes are counted above.

entries.title: The Shield
entries.heading: What it costs
entries.text: The defendant bears the cost of the timing rule.

entries.title: Findings About People
entries.heading: What it costs
entries.text: The person under a finding bears the restriction while it stays in force.

entries.title: Findings About People
entries.heading: What it costs
entries.text: Compromised reviewers and historical witnesses can agree on false accounts, and a subject found against on such an account bears the finding until an appeal ends it.

entries.title: The One Thing Taken
entries.heading: Argument: A power that takes movement and then expires
entries.text: Against abolition my rule costs the people confined and those who depend on them: time, and the job, tenancy or care that retained legal rights leave exposed in practice, the loss Norway's previously employed defendants suffered.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: A denial of contact that no authorised independent witness records stays unmarked, and the person held bears that wait; routine review and the complaint route are what remain to them.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because a disagreement between the witness and the reviewer blocks the finding, an honest dispute about the period withholds the marker from the person it concerns for as long as it lasts.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: And because the placement alarm reads reports, a misplacement nobody reports raises no alarm, and the person misplaced bears it.

entries.title: The Child With Nobody
entries.heading: Argument: Standing before identity
entries.text: My rule puts the cost on whoever funds provision, and in a real shortage on other claimants: provision will sometimes reach a duplicate or a false name, because the rules accept an encounter's name without authenticating it.

entries.title: When There Is Genuinely Not Enough
entries.heading: Argument: A shortage must be proved, and need decides it
entries.text: Some allocations will save fewer years than a benefit-maximising rule, and the loss falls on claimants whose longer expected lives would have won.

entries.title: The Same Route for Everyone
entries.heading: Argument: Effects, adjustments and measures that end
entries.text: Their cost falls on applicants outside a measure who would have won a contested place; proof by effect costs providers, whose neutral practices must pass the tests for indirect distinctions.

costs.title: People forgoing a gain or livelihood

entries.title: A Place in Which Life Remains Possible
entries.heading: Argument: Conditions kept apart
entries.text: An activity that would raise welfare on the whole remains a breach if it fails one condition, and the people who would have gained bear that.

entries.title: A Place in Which Life Remains Possible
entries.heading: Argument: Conditions kept apart
entries.text: A Guardian's pause delays the irreversible part of an authorised activity, a delay its proponent and those awaiting its benefits bear.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: People whose livelihoods or diets rest on animal food bear the food rule.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: A community whose practice reaches the core gains no exemption.

entries.title: Whether It Arrived
entries.heading: Argument: Evidence from the person served
entries.text: Its cost falls on honest providers, who must find a witness; on whoever pays for witnesses; and on everyone owed an honest record, because a witness who colludes with a provider passes, where a presence check would at least demand the recipient.

entries.title: The Same Route for Everyone
entries.heading: Argument: Effects, adjustments and measures that end
entries.text: Their cost falls on applicants outside a measure who would have won a contested place; proof by effect costs providers, whose neutral practices must pass the tests for indirect distinctions.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: Owners, farmers, researchers and households lose the power to settle an animal's interests and must justify every food, research, lethal, invasive or high-severity use against its alternatives.

entries.title: The Child With Nobody
entries.heading: Argument: Standing before identity
entries.text: My rule puts the cost on whoever funds provision, and in a real shortage on other claimants: provision will sometimes reach a duplicate or a false name, because the rules accept an encounter's name without authenticating it.

entries.title: What You Are Owed
entries.heading: Argument: Owed to everyone, by someone
entries.text: That costs what the conditional duty saves, and whoever funds the common tier pays for a debt owed also to people who could feed themselves.

entries.title: Whether It Arrived
entries.heading: Argument: Evidence from the person served
entries.text: Its cost falls on honest providers, who must find a witness; on whoever pays for witnesses; and on everyone owed an honest record, because a witness who colludes with a provider passes, where a presence check would at least demand the recipient.

entries.title: Who Owes, and What Follows
entries.heading: Argument: Named bearers, and a court that secures the minimum
entries.text: The Assembly loses the power to trade the minimum against other goods, the first claim on funds presses on every other claim, and a minimum fixed in the constitution binds even where it proves ill-suited, as Mazibuko feared.

entries.title: Work, Pay and Contribution
entries.heading: Argument: Work above the floor
entries.text: Some people able to work will choose otherwise and keep the floor, whoever funds the floor pays for them, and the design gives up whatever push into work a sanction brings.

entries.title: What Money Cannot Buy
entries.heading: Argument: Ownership under the floor, borrowing under law
entries.text: My choice costs later taxpayers, who pay for debt an earlier majority chose, and the services above the floor, which compete with debt service.

entries.title: A Way to Be Heard
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because a request from anyone creates a review duty, review offices owe answers to weak requests as well as strong ones, and whoever funds them pays for both.

entries.title: A Prisoner Is a Person
entries.heading: Argument: Liberty is what a sentence takes
entries.text: The public owes the whole floor to people who have harmed others, the gravest offender included, at the level it owes the people they harmed, and those people must accept it.

entries.title: Where People Are Put
entries.heading: Argument: Proved harm opens the harshest place
entries.text: Two people convicted of the same offence may be held in different places, and the offices must make findings a category would supply at a stroke, at public cost.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because every complaint about custody conditions creates a duty to investigate and every confined person is owed routine review, the review body answers weak complaints as well as strong ones, and whoever funds it pays for both.

entries.title: What Nobody Has to Ask Permission For
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: A restricting body must assemble evidence, three agreeing attesters, reasons and review before it acts, and the people a restriction would protect wait while it does; while a challenge suspends the restriction, they wait again.

entries.title: What Nobody Has to Ask Permission For
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: A protective record binds a body on one source's word, before any review, and the body bears those duties unless a reviewer withdraws them.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Staggered, nonrenewable mandates mean that a new majority reaches the membership of a court or oversight body only as seats fall due, and that an experienced holder leaves when a mandate ends.

entries.title: A Crisis Does Not Suspend the Republic
entries.heading: Argument: Four powers and every right in force
entries.text: Each renewal and each measure needs its own period and review, so reviewers must keep pace with the crisis.

entries.title: A Way to Be Heard
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because a request from anyone creates a review duty, review offices owe answers to weak requests as well as strong ones, and whoever funds them pays for both.

entries.title: Where People Are Put
entries.heading: Argument: Proved harm opens the harshest place
entries.text: Two people convicted of the same offence may be held in different places, and the offices must make findings a category would supply at a stroke, at public cost.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because isolation is marked only by a positive finding from two actors outside the holding, the holder can sign neither part of a finding about its own holding, and every finding waits for people from outside.

entries.title: When the System Notices It Broke
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Because every complaint about custody conditions creates a duty to investigate and every confined person is owed routine review, the review body answers weak complaints as well as strong ones, and whoever funds it pays for both.

entries.title: Who Owes, and What Follows
entries.heading: Argument: Named bearers, and a court that secures the minimum
entries.text: The Assembly loses the power to trade the minimum against other goods, the first claim on funds presses on every other claim, and a minimum fixed in the constitution binds even where it proves ill-suited, as Mazibuko feared.

entries.title: A Place in Which Life Remains Possible
entries.heading: Argument: Conditions kept apart
entries.text: A later majority that judges a commons axis worth trading for prosperity cannot make the trade, however large it is.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Equal regional weight gives a resident of a small region more indirect weight than a resident of a large one when the Council decides a regional settlement.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: A government that has lost the Assembly's support stays in office until a majority agrees on its successor, and the public lives under it meanwhile.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Who bears the cost
entries.text: Staggered, nonrenewable mandates mean that a new majority reaches the membership of a court or oversight body only as seats fall due, and that an experienced holder leaves when a mandate ends.

entries.title: How Public Power Is Built
entries.heading: Argument: Divided without deadlock
entries.text: The price falls on the identifiable people counted above, and on a voter seeking whom to punish, who finds a council and an Assembly majority.

entries.title: A Crisis Does Not Suspend the Republic
entries.heading: Argument: Four powers and every right in force
entries.text: Against Ackerman, a renewal renews the same four powers however large its majority; broader consent buys no broader power, and whoever a wider measure would have protected bears that.

entries.title: Changing the Rules
entries.heading: Argument: A fixed core behind an open route
entries.text: My choice costs a later majority, however large and lasting, that wants to change what the core protects.

entries.title: Changing the Rules
entries.heading: Argument: A fixed core behind an open route
entries.text: Reformers with majority support can be blocked by more than a third of the Assembly.

entries.title: Creatures Without a Ballot
entries.heading: Argument: A claim of its own
entries.text: The cost falls on animals: a domesticated animal gains no say in its society, and a wild population is protected through its habitat and the commons rather than as a community of its own.

entries.title: Arriving and Belonging
entries.heading: Argument: The person before the status
entries.text: A former resident who made a home abroad loses the vote in the place left behind, and people outside the republic whom its decisions affect gain no vote there.
